initiative.title: Coax Nostr: our own Nostr stack, crypto included, in Coax
initiative.body: Every Nostr integration on openagents.com runs in Coax: SHA-256, secp256k1, BIP-340, ECDH, NIP-44, NIP-59, events, bech32, relay client. Specification: coax/nostr.md.

milestones.title: Hashes and ciphers
milestones.body: Byte helpers, SHA-256, HMAC, HKDF, PBKDF2, ChaCha20, hex and base64 in Coax, each against its official vectors.

milestones.title: Field and scalar arithmetic
milestones.body: secp256k1 field elements (10×26) and scalars mod n, with inversion and square root, proven bounds and differential tests.

milestones.title: Group arithmetic and Schnorr verify
milestones.body: Points, wNAF dual multiplication and BIP-340 verification.

milestones.title: Signing and ECDH
milestones.body: Fixed-base comb, constant-time ladder, BIP-340 signing and x-only ECDH, with timing evidence.

milestones.title: NIP-44 and NIP-59
milestones.body: Version 2 encryption, seals and gift wraps that interoperate with spec implementations.

milestones.title: Events and encodings
milestones.body: Bounded JSON, NIP-01 events, filters, bech32 and NIP-19, JCS and the 3188 artifact envelope.

milestones.title: A relay client in the page
milestones.body: Host random, socket and storage imports; the relay state machine with NIP-42 AUTH.

milestones.title: Replace the TypeScript
milestones.body: The hidden deck opens with no TypeScript: opener, gate, sealer and injector in Coax; the INVARIANTS change.

milestones.title: The project page goes live
milestones.body: /project/coax reads its project, tasks and order from the relay and signs claims in the page.

milestones.title: Coax compiler prerequisites
milestones.body: Small compiler features and fixes the stack wants; none blocks M0–M2.

milestones.title: Sign in to the website with your phone
milestones.body: The deliverable: open openagents.com/signin, scan its QR code with the OpenAgents mobile app, approve, and the website is signed in as your Nostr key. The key never leaves the phone. NIP-46 (Nostr Connect) between page and phone over relay.openagents.com, NIP-98 HTTP auth to the server, no WorkOS. The same Coax Nostr library runs on the phone (compiled to C), in the page (wasm) and on the server (native).

tasks.title: Compound assignment through a view emits valid C
tasks.body: `t[0].count[b] += 1` on an array field reached through a view generates C that does not compile (found building the project page). Fix the emitter and add a regression test.
acceptance: A test with `t[0].count[b] += 1` (and -=, *=, |=) through a view compiles and runs under ASan
coax/tests pass

tasks.title: A value_barrier intrinsic for constant-time code
tasks.body: Add `value_barrier(x: u64) -> u64` (and u32) that the optimizer cannot see through: native emits `__asm__("" : "+r"(x))`, wasm32 emits a call to a non-inlined identity. Document it in coax/spec.md §9.
acceptance: Generated C for a masked select compiled with clang -O2 contains no conditional branch on the masked value (checked by objdump in a test script)
coax/tests pass

tasks.title: Explicit wrapping add and rotate for u32 and u64
tasks.body: Add `add_wrap`, `sub_wrap`, `mul_wrap`, `rotl`, `rotr` for u32/u64 that never trap in any build mode. SHA-256 and ChaCha20 can use them instead of computing in u64 and masking.
acceptance: Tests for each op at the type's limits in debug and --release
coax/tests pass

tasks.title: mul_wide: a 64×64→128 multiply as two u64 halves
tasks.body: Add `mul_wide(a, b: u64) -> (hi, lo: u64)`: C emits `unsigned __int128`; wasm32 emits a four-multiply split. Enables a 5×52 field on native later.
acceptance: Random and edge vectors match a reference computed with __int128 on native and in wasm32 (node or a headless page)
coax/tests pass

tasks.title: Debug-only struct fields and checks
tasks.body: A way to declare fields and statements that exist only in development builds (spec §10.5 conditional compilation, the minimal slice), so field elements can carry magnitudes in debug and not in release.
acceptance: A struct with a debug-only field has a smaller size_of in --release; statements under the debug condition are absent from release C
coax/tests pass

tasks.title: Byte helpers: big/little-endian loads, constant-time equality, select and zeroize
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/bytes.coax: load/store be32/le32/be64/le64, ct_eq over views (returns a mask), ct_select for u32/u64 and views, zeroize through the value barrier (a #foreign no-op until the intrinsic lands).
acceptance: #test covers every helper at boundaries
coax mutate coax/lib/crypto/bytes.coax: no surviving mutants

tasks.title: Pin the official test vectors with their sources and hashes
tasks.body: Create coax/tests/vectors/ with the files listed in coax/nostr.md §9.1 (NIST SHA-256 subset, RFC 4231, 5869, 7914, 8439, BIP-340 CSV, Wycheproof ecdh_secp256k1, NIP-44 vectors, BIP-173) and SOURCES.md recording URL, retrieval date and SHA-256 of each.
acceptance: Every file in SOURCES.md matches its recorded SHA-256 (a check script)
No file is modified from upstream

tasks.title: A native vector runner for Coax crypto modules
tasks.body: tools/coax-nostr/vectors.sh builds each module with `coax c` → clang with ASan/UBSan and runs a C driver per vector file, reporting pass/fail per row. Heavy vectors run here; small ones also run as #test.
acceptance: Runs on macOS with the existing toolchain
Fails loudly on a single wrong row (tested by corrupting one expected value in a temp copy)

tasks.title: SHA-256, streaming and one-shot, with the BIP-340 tagged hash
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/sha256.coax: init/update/final over views, one-shot sha256, and tagged_hash(tag, msg) = SHA256(SHA256(tag)||SHA256(tag)||msg) with the three BIP-340 tags' prefixes precomputed with #run.
acceptance: NIST subset and the 1 MiB split-at-every-chunk test pass in the vector runner
#test: empty, "abc", tagged hash of BIP0340/challenge known value
coax mutate: no surviving mutants
≥ 150 MB/s in wasm32, ≥ 300 MB/s native (bench printed)

tasks.title: HMAC-SHA256 and HKDF
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/hmac.coax and hkdf.coax: hmac_sha256(key, msg), HKDF extract and expand (NIP-44 uses expand with 76 bytes).
acceptance: RFC 4231 cases 1–7 and RFC 5869 cases 1–3 pass
coax mutate: no surviving mutants

tasks.title: PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/pbkdf2.coax for the phrase gate (210,000 rounds); reuse the HMAC inner/outer state per round.
acceptance: RFC 7914 §11 vectors pass
210,000 rounds take under 400 ms in wasm32 in Chrome

tasks.title: ChaCha20 block function and stream cipher

acceptance: coax mutate: no surviving mutants
≥ 250 MB/s in wasm32

tasks.title: Bounded hex and base64 codecs
tasks.body: coax/lib/nostr/hex.coax and base64.coax (standard alphabet, with padding, as NIP-44 uses): encode and strict decode into caller buffers; refuse bad characters, bad padding and overflow.
acceptance: RFC 4648 §10 vectors pass
Every invalid NIP-44 base64 case is refused
coax mutate: no surviving mutants

tasks.title: Field elements in 10×26 limbs: load, store, normalize, add, negate
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/secp_field.coax: the representation, set_b32 (refusing ≥ p where asked), get_b32, normalize (constant time), add, negate with magnitude parameter, mul_int, is_zero, equal. Debug magnitude/normalized tracking.
acceptance: #test round-trips for 0, 1, p−1, 2^256−1 mod p and limb-boundary values
Magnitude violations trap in debug builds (negative tests)

tasks.title: Field multiply and square with compile-time bound proofs
tasks.body: mul and sqr with reduction by 2^256 ≡ 2^32 + 977; #run/#assert prove the largest accumulator stays below 2^64 for inputs of magnitude ≤ 8.
acceptance: The bound #assert fails to compile if the admitted magnitude is raised to 9 (documented negative check)
1,000,000 random products match a native libsecp256k1 harness
coax mutate: no surviving mutants

tasks.title: Field inversion and square root with fixed addition chains
tasks.body: inv (a^(p−2)) and sqrt (a^((p+1)/4), returning whether a root exists), constant time, plus inv_vartime for public inputs (may initially call inv).
acceptance: a·inv(a) = 1 for 100,000 random a; sqrt(a²) = ±a; non-residues refused
Matches libsecp harness on edge values

tasks.title: Scalars mod n in 8×32 limbs
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/secp_scalar.coax: set_b32 with overflow flag, get_b32, add, mul, negate, inverse, is_zero, constant-time cond_negate, and bit/window extraction for multiplication.
acceptance: Edge values (0, 1, n−1, n, 2^256−1) and 1,000,000 random ops match the libsecp harness
coax mutate: no surviving mutants

tasks.title: A differential harness against libsecp256k1
tasks.body: tools/coax-nostr/fuzz/: fetch libsecp256k1 at a pinned tag (verify tarball hash), build it with the harness only, expose field/scalar/point/schnorr/ecdh comparisons to C drivers that call our modules. Never vendored into the tree.
acceptance: `tools/coax-nostr/fuzz/run.sh field 60` runs 60 s with no disagreement on a correct build and finds a planted bug
Tarball hash pinned and checked

tasks.title: Points: affine and Jacobian add, double and mixed add
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/secp_group.coax: infinity handling, gej_double, gej_add_ge (mixed), gej_add, ge_set_gej, set_xo (lift x with even y, BIP-340), is_valid_xo, and constant-time table selection ge_table_select.
acceptance: Generator multiples 1..1000 match the harness
Doubling/adding at infinity and P + (−P) correct
coax mutate: no surviving mutants

tasks.title: wNAF dual multiplication a·G + b·P for verification
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/secp_mult.coax: ecmult_vartime(a, P, b) using wNAF (window 5 for P, a precomputed G table generated with #run). Public inputs only; name ends _vartime.
acceptance: 100,000 random (a, P, b) match the harness
Precomputed table generated at compile time within the step budget

tasks.title: BIP-340 Schnorr verification
tasks.body: coax/lib/crypto/schnorr.coax: verify(sig64, msg32, xonly32) per BIP-340, refusing r ≥ p, s ≥ n and invalid public keys.
acceptance: Every verification row of BIP-340 test-vectors.csv (pass and fail) matches

acceptance: 100,000 random k match the harness
Timing harness |t| < 4.5 over 10^6 runs, fixed vs random k, native

tasks.body: A fixed-window (4-bit) constant-time multiplication for ECDH, with signed-digit recoding and masked table selection.
acceptance: 100,000 random (k, P) match the harness
Timing harness |t| < 4.5, native

acceptance: Every signing row of BIP-340 test-vectors.csv matches byte for byte

acceptance: Opens wraps made by today's coax/web/unlock/seal.ts and by nostr-effect nip44+pure
Wraps it makes open with nostr-effect nip44+pure

tasks.title: /project/coax reads its project, tasks and order from the relay
tasks.body: The real project page holds a WebSocket to relay.openagents.com and redraws as events arrive: no snapshots, no release needed to show a claim, a plan, a note, a status or a reorder. The host only moves bytes (host-socket-pipe); Coax parses the relay's JSON, keeps the project's events (REQ with authors = the project key; the relay checks signatures until project-page-verify lands), folds them the way coax/web/project/model.ts does (issues, revisions, statuses, claims, releases, plans, notes, commits, the order record) into the tables project.coax draws, and redraws. Subscriptions stay open after EOSE so new events land live; reconnect with backoff; the header shows LIVE, CONNECTING or OFFLINE instead of a snapshot time. The build-time tables stay only as the first paint until the socket's first EOSE. The demo page keeps its samples.
acceptance: A claim, a plan update and a done published with publish.ts show on the production page within 2 s, with no release
Moving a task (publish.ts move) reorders the live page within 2 s
#test: the Coax fold of a captured relay transcript equals model.ts fold() of the same events (same rows, order, plans, log)
Killing the socket shows OFFLINE, and it reconnects with backoff
No TypeScript beyond the host byte pipe; check-visuals passes

tasks.title: The live project page verifies every event in Coax
